question: What is the primary function of controlling in nursing management?

options.A: To create initial patient care budgets
options.B: To ensure actual performance conforms to planned goals
options.C: To hire new nursing personnel for clinical units
options.D: To schedule daily staff shifts and ward rotations

explanation: Controlling is the management function that ensures actual organizational performance aligns with planned goals and objectives. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: What serves as the benchmark against which nursing care outcomes are measured in a healthcare facility?
explanation: Standards serve as the benchmark or yardstick against which nursing care outcomes and operational practices are measured. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why are performance standards particularly important in Nigerian hospitals with high nurse-to-patient ratios?

options.A: They help prioritize essential care tasks and maintain patient safety
options.B: They automatically increase the number of available nurses
options.C: They eliminate the need for patient documentation
options.D: They replace the need for hospital management

explanation: Clear performance standards help prioritize essential care tasks and maintain patient safety, especially in high-workload environments. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: How do performance standards assist nursing managers during staff appraisals?

options.A: By providing objective criteria for evaluating staff competence and behavior
options.B: By determining the exact salary increases for every worker
options.C: By deciding which staff members should resign
options.D: By eliminating the need to observe clinical work

explanation: Performance standards form the objective foundation for staff appraisals and evaluating professional competence. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a quantitative nursing standard?

options.C: Level of empathy shown during counseling
options.D: Perceived comfort of the ward environment

explanation: Quantitative standards focus on measurable numerical data like the length of a patient's stay, staffing ratios, and infection rates. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of qualitative standards in healthcare?

options.A: Counting the exact number of daily admissions
options.B: Assessing subjective aspects like empathy and patient satisfaction
options.C: Measuring the precise speed of medication delivery

explanation: Qualitative standards evaluate subjective aspects of care, such as patient satisfaction, empathy, and communication effectiveness. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why must nursing standards be realistic and achievable?

options.A: To ensure they reflect available resources and prevent staff demotivation
options.B: To make sure nurses never have to work overtime
options.C: To eliminate the need for hospital equipment
options.D: To guarantee that every patient leaves the hospital in one day

explanation: Standards must reflect available resources and staffing levels; setting impossible benchmarks only demotivates healthcare staff. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: What does it mean for a nursing standard to be evidence-based?

options.A: It is based on old hospital traditions and personal opinions
options.B: It is grounded in current nursing research and clinical guidelines
options.C: It is written exclusively by hospital financial accountants
options.D: It changes randomly every single shift

explanation: Evidence-based standards are grounded in current nursing research and established clinical guidelines rather than outdated traditions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: Who should be involved in reviewing drafted clinical standards to ensure practical feasibility?

options.B: Frontline nurses, doctors, and allied health professionals
options.C: Hospital security guards and administrative accountants

explanation: Frontline staff who will implement the standards must review them to ensure buy-in and practical feasibility in daily clinical workflows. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: What is the final phase in the established process of clinical standard setting?

options.A: Continuous monitoring and periodic review of the standards
options.B: Immediate dismissal of staff who fail to read the manual
options.C: Halting all patient admissions until perfection is reached
options.D: Destroying all previous hospital medical records

explanation: Continuous monitoring and periodic review ensure that standards remain dynamic, relevant, and updated with new evidence. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h5)

question: Which statutory body in Nigeria sets the legal scope of practice and professional code of conduct for nurses?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives (NANNM)
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN) is the statutory body responsible for setting the legal scope of practice and codes of conduct. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: What is a primary purpose of regulatory guidelines in nursing practice?

options.A: To protect the public by ensuring nurses are licensed and competent
options.B: To restrict nurses from ever speaking with patients
options.C: To replace the need for hospital administrative structures
options.D: To increase the cost of nursing education programs

explanation: Regulatory frameworks protect the public by ensuring every practicing nurse is licensed, competent, and ethically sound. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h6)

question: How do severe nurse shortages and heavy workloads negatively impact standard implementation?

options.A: They lead to burnout and tempt nurses to take shortcuts that compromise protocols
options.B: They automatically provide more time for patient documentation
options.C: They eliminate the need for any clinical supervision
options.D: They increase the availability of modern medical equipment

explanation: Heavy workloads and nurse shortages cause burnout, which can lead staff to take clinical shortcuts that compromise protocols. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: What is a major psychological hurdle when introducing new evidence-based standards in clinical units?

options.A: Excessive enthusiasm from every single staff member
options.B: Resistance to change from staff accustomed to traditional routines
options.C: Immediate compliance without any questions asked
options.D: Complete elimination of all hospital paperwork

explanation: Resistance to change from staff who prefer traditional routines over new evidence-based practices is a common barrier. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h7)

question: What methods do nurse managers use to assess how closely clinical practice matches established standards?

options.A: Observational audits, chart reviews, and patient feedback surveys
options.B: Ignoring daily ward activities and waiting for annual reports
options.C: Relying purely on staff personal feelings without data collection
options.D: Stopping all patient care to conduct financial audits

explanation: Systematic data collection, observational audits, chart reviews, and patient surveys are key methods used to evaluate compliance with standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h8)

question: What should a nurse manager do first when a discrepancy or substandard practice is identified during monitoring?

options.A: Immediately fire the entire nursing staff on duty
options.B: Investigate the root causes of the discrepancy
options.C: Delete the established standard from the hospital manual
options.D: Hide the incident report from the hospital board

explanation: Managers must investigate the root causes of deviations—such as training gaps or resource shortages—rather than resorting immediately to punishment. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h8)
